Formulas on the Web

Pages write formulas in MathML, which browsers lay out themselves, or have a script such as KaTeX or MathJax typeset them from LaTeX. Reader mode lays out the MathML they leave behind, and a formula becomes a run of text in its linear notation for search and copy.

Plain MathML: the area of a circle is A=πr2, and its circumference C=2πr. A formula on its own line:

∑n=1∞ 1n2 = π26

KaTeX writes the MathML beside HTML of its own, which a style sheet hides from sight: f(x)=1−x2f(x) = \sqrt{1 - x^2}f(x) and Wikipedia a picture of the formula beside hidden MathML: detA=|abcd|=ad−bc.

MathJax 2 keeps the LaTeX in scripts, which it typesets where they are:

The text around a formula wraps as it would around a word, and the lines grow to hold formulas taller than the text.
